# Part 1: Data verification & tidy data

## 1.1 Data import

Keep only Sample id plus what verification, grouping and Part 2's figures
actually use - `ST`/`Serotype` renamed and coerced to character here so
nothing downstream touches the raw `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type` /
`SeroTypeFinder/SeroType` names again.

A note: I only verified/asked questions for the spelling and re-encoding - for the fields that are included in the downstream figures (or kept in this data)
ST, Serotype, Production, Species

```{r load data}
isolates_raw <- read_excel(
  here::here(params$results_xlsx),
  sheet = params$isolate_sheet
) %>%
  select(
    Sample, Year, 
    Case = sak,
    ST = `mlst_scheme_list/sequence_type`,
    Serotype = `SeroTypeFinder/SeroType`,
    Production = driftsformnavn,
    Species = artnavn
  ) %>%
  mutate(ST = as.character(ST))
```

```{r initial glimpse}
glimpse(isolates_raw)
```

## 1.2 Completeness checks

One row per isolate, and the fields every downstream figure depends on
(year, ST, serotype, production type) must be complete.

```{r qc checks}
qc <- list(
  n_rows = nrow(isolates_raw),
  n_distinct_sample = n_distinct(isolates_raw$Sample),
  n_missing_year = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Year)),
  n_missing_case = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Case)),
  n_missing_ST = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$ST)),
  n_missing_serotype = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Serotype)),
  n_missing_production = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Production)),
  n_missing_species = sum(is.na(isolates_raw$Species))
  )

qc

stopifnot(
  "one row per isolate expected" = qc$n_rows == qc$n_distinct_sample,
  "Year must be complete" = qc$n_missing_year == 0,
  "ST must be complete" = qc$n_missing_ST == 0,
  "Serotype must be complete" = qc$n_missing_serotype == 0,
  "Production must be complete" = qc$n_missing_production == 0
)
```

## 1.3 Category spelling / homogeneity check


`check_spelling_homogeneity()` flags pairs of values in a column that are
identical after trimming/casefolding ("case_or_whitespace" - safe to
auto-fix) or within a small edit distance ("possible_typo" - needs a human
read).

Tolerance differs by column: `Production`/`Species` are free text, so a
1-2 character difference is almost always a typo (`max_dist = 2`); `ST`/
`Serotype` are nomenclature codes where a 1-character difference is usually a
genuinely different code (`O1:H4` vs. `O1:H7`), so only exact
case/whitespace collisions are flagged (`max_dist = 0`).

```{r spelling checks}
spelling_flags <- bind_rows(
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Production, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Production"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Species, max_dist = 2) %>% mutate(column = "Species"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$ST, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "ST"),
  check_spelling_homogeneity(isolates_raw$Serotype, max_dist = 0) %>% mutate(column = "Serotype")
) %>%
  relocate(column)

spelling_flags

write_csv(spelling_flags, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "spelling_flags.csv"))
```

Findings, fixed below: `Production` has a known mojibake artifact
("Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon" vs. corrupted "Foreldredyr,
kj�ttproduksjon", 2 rows); `Species` has one genuine case duplicate
("Rowan ranger" vs. "Rowan Ranger" - the other near-neighbours are real,
distinct breed names and are correctly not flagged); `ST`/`Serotype` have
nothing flagged.

```{r fix flagged values}
isolates_fixed <- isolates_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Production = if_else(
      Production == "Foreldredyr, kj�ttproduksjon",
      "Foreldredyr, kjøttproduksjon",
      Production)
    )
```

## 1.4 Cleaning: production type (broiler / parent flock)
And transforming Norwegian to English 
```{r clean driftsform}
isolates <- isolates_fixed %>%
  mutate(
    production_type = case_when(
      str_starts(Production, "Foreldredyr") ~ "Parent flock",
      Production == "Kjøttproduksjon" ~ "Broiler",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    production_type = factor(production_type, levels = c("Broiler", "Parent flock")),
    Year = as.integer(Year)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Species = case_when(
        Species == "Høns" ~ "Chicken",
        Species == "Hubbard" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Hubbard JA 787" ~ "Hubbard",
        Species == "Ross" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross 308" ~ "Ross 308",
        Species == "Ross rowan" ~ "Ross rowan",
        Species == "Rowan 308" ~ "Rowan 308",
        Species == "Rowan Ranger" ~ "Rowan ranger",
        Species == "Rustic gold" ~ "Rustic gold",
        Species == "Sasso" ~ "Sasso",
        TRUE ~ Species
      ),
      Species = factor(Species, levels = c(
        "Chicken",  "Ross 308", "Hubbard", "Ross rowan", "Rowan 308", "Rowan ranger", "Rustic gold", "Sasso")
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-Production)

stopifnot("production_type must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$production_type)) == 0)
stopifnot("Species must be complete after recoding" = sum(is.na(isolates$Species)) == 0)
count(isolates, production_type)
count(isolates, Species)

```

## 1.5 New variable: `variant` (ST-Serotype combination)

Requested format: `ST23-O78:H4`.

```{r variant column}
isolates <- isolates %>%
  mutate(
    ST = paste0("ST", ST),
    variant = paste0(ST, "-", Serotype)
    )

n_distinct(isolates$variant)  # 134 distinct ST-Serotype combinations observed
head(count(isolates, variant, sort = TRUE), 5)
```

## 1.6 ST, Serotype, variant contingency tables evaluation - top 5 / top 10

Same question, two groupings: keep the top N *variants*, how many distinct
ST/Serotype does that represent; keep the top N *ST*s instead, how many
distinct Serotype/variant. Same `top_n_contingency()` +
`summarise_contingency()` pattern for both, just a different `group_col` /
`other_cols` - shared helpers (`kept_vs_other()`, `total_distinct_values()`,
`add_proportions()`, all in `code/R/`) do the rest, one subsection each.

```{r contingency helpers}
# how many distinct values of ST/Serotype/variant exist overall, to turn
# n_distinct_values (below) into a percentage of "how much of the diversity"
total_distinct <- total_distinct_values(isolates, c("ST", "Serotype", "variant"))
total_distinct
```

### Grouped by variant

```{r top n variant contingency}
variant_contingency_top5 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 5, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype"))
variant_contingency_top10 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "variant", top_n = 10, other_cols = c("ST", "Serotype"))

variant_threshold_summary <- bind_rows(
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top5, 5),
  kept_vs_other(variant_contingency_top10, 10)
) %>%
  add_proportions(total_distinct, nrow(isolates))

write_tsv(variant_threshold_summary, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "variant_threshold_summary.tsv"))

variant_threshold_summary
```

Reading this: keeping the top 5 variants covers 417/884 isolates (47.2%) but
names only 5/88 STs (5.7%) and 5/115 serotypes (4.3%) - the "other" bucket is
the minority of isolates (467, 52.8%) yet holds nearly all of the diversity
(97.7% of STs, 99.1% of serotypes). Top 10 covers more isolates (550/884,
62.2%) at a similar diversity trade-off - 8 STs (9.1%) and 10 serotypes
(8.7%) named, 94.3%/95.7% still in "other". Neither threshold captures much
ST/Serotype diversity - that's inherent to a "top N" cut on data this skewed
(one variant, ST23-O78:H4, is 244/884 isolates - 27.6% - on its own), not a
flaw in the threshold choice.

### Grouped by ST

```{r top n ST contingency}
ST_contingency_top5 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "ST", top_n = 5, other_cols = c("Serotype", "variant"))
ST_contingency_top10 <- top_n_contingency(isolates, "ST", top_n = 10, other_cols = c("Serotype", "variant"))

ST_threshold_summary <- bind_rows(
  kept_vs_other(ST_contingency_top5, 5),
  kept_vs_other(ST_contingency_top10, 10)
) %>%
  add_proportions(total_distinct, nrow(isolates))

write_tsv(ST_threshold_summary, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "ST_threshold_summary.tsv"))

ST_threshold_summary
```

Reading this: grouping by ST instead captures more diversity per isolate,
because one ST can carry several different serotypes. Top 5 STs cover
505/884 isolates (57.1%) and represent 18/115 serotypes (15.7%) and 19/134
variants (14.2%) - roughly 3-4x the serotype/variant coverage of the top-5
*variant* grouping, for a similar isolate share. "Other" (379 isolates,
42.9%) still holds most of the diversity (103 serotypes, 89.6%; 115
variants, 85.8%). Top 10 STs: 645/884 isolates (73.0%), 23 serotypes (20.0%),
25 variants (18.7%) named; 239 other isolates (27.0%) still cover 98
serotypes (85.2%) and 109 variants (81.3%).

## Preparing for figures 

### Fig 7 - Pie Matrix

#### top 5 variants


```{r grouped columns}
top5_variants_fig7_prep <- 
  isolates %>%
  mutate(
    variant_top5 = top_n_other(variant, 5, other_label = "Other"),
    Serotype_label_variant_top5 = ifelse(variant_top5 == "Other", "Other", Serotype),
    ST_label_variant_top5 = ifelse(variant_top5 == "Other", "Other", ST),
  )
```

Now preparing data for visualisation
```{r getting contingency table for top5 variants fig 7}
top5_variants_fig7 <-
  top5_variants_fig7_prep %>%
  select(Year, variant_top5, production_type) %>%
  group_by(Year, variant_top5, production_type) %>%
  tally()

top5_variants_fig7
write_tsv(top5_variants_fig7, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "fig7_top5_variant_year_production_tally.tsv"))
```

This is the data we use to produce the figure


```{r figure7 top5 pie data}
# x order: top 5 by total isolate count (desc), "Other" always last
variant_top5_totals <- 
  top5_variants_fig7 %>%
  group_by(variant_top5) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total))

variant_top5_totals

variant_top5_levels <- c(setdiff(variant_top5_totals$variant_top5, "Other"), "Other")
variant_top5_levels

x_spacing <- 1.7  # > 1 spaces the variant columns further apart, widening the
                  # plot; coord_equal() keeps pies round regardless (spacing
                  # is between x positions, not a change to their unit scale)
fig7_top5_pie_data <-
  top5_variants_fig7 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = production_type, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(
    variant_top5 = factor(variant_top5, levels = variant_top5_levels),
    x = as.numeric(variant_top5) * x_spacing,
    y = Year,
    total = Broiler + `Parent flock`
  )

fig7_top5_pie_data 
# area-proportional radius (not radius-proportional - r ∝ sqrt(total), so
# doubling isolate count does not double the radius, it doubles the area)
max_total <- max(fig7_top5_pie_data$total)
fig7_top5_pie_data <- 
  fig7_top5_pie_data %>%
  mutate(r = 0.42 * sqrt(total / max_total))

fig7_top5_pie_data
```

r = 0.42 * sqrt(total / max_total)
Computes each pie's radius. This is built to make circle area — not radius — proportional to isolate count - as humans percive circle size best by area. 

<!-- Explanations:
total / max_total → 189 / 189 = 1. This normalizes every count to a 0–1 scale, where 1 = the biggest cell in the whole dataset (whatever that happens to be — right now it's the same 189, since max_total is derived from fig7_top5_pie_data itself).
sqrt(1) = 1. For a smaller cell, e.g. 50 isolates: sqrt(50/189) = sqrt(0.265) = 0.514 — note this is not 50/189 = 0.265; the square root pulls smaller values up relative to a straight ratio, which is exactly what's needed to compensate for area growing quadratically.
0.42 * 1 = 0.42. The 0.42 is just a scale factor — "the biggest pie gets a radius of 0.42 data-units" — chosen by eye so the largest circle (ST23-O78:H4/2021) fits within one x/y grid cell (columns and years are 1 unit apart, so a radius approaching 0.5 would make adjacent pies touch).
--> 

```{r figure7 top5 pie}
# save dimensions - fixed here (not just passed to save_apec_plot below)
# because the legend calibration two steps down needs to know the exact
# physical size the panel will render at; if these change, the plot must be
# rebuilt (calibrate -> plot) for the legend to stay correct - they can't
# drift apart since both read from the same two variables.
fig7_width_cm <- 32
fig7_height_cm <- 18

# the real pies (below) already carry a correct, data-coordinate radius (r).
# For the "Isolate number" legend we want a REAL ggplot legend (so it joins
# Production type's legend box, positioned automatically) - but a real
# legend's `size` aesthetic is in mm, an entirely different unit system from
# `r`'s data-coordinates, with no fixed relationship between them. Fix: render
# the plot once off-screen at its real save size, measure how many mm one
# data-unit actually occupies in the rendered, coord_equal() panel
# (panel_mm_per_data_unit(), code/R/viz/), and use that to calibrate
# scale_size_area()'s max_size so the legend's circles are the same physical
# size as the real pies - not just at the endpoint (189), but everywhere,
# since scale_size_area() applies the identical sqrt(value/max) transform
# used for `r` below.
base_plot <-
  ggplot() +
  geom_scatterpie(
    data = fig7_top5_pie_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y, r = r),
    cols = c("Broiler", "Parent flock"),
    color = NA
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(variant_top5_levels) * x_spacing, labels = variant_top5_levels, expand = expansion(add = 0.7)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(fig7_top5_pie_data$Year)), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2], name = "Production type") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 variants (ST-Serotype), by year",
    x = "Variant", y = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_apec_piematrix()

mm_per_unit <- panel_mm_per_data_unit(base_plot, fig7_width_cm, fig7_height_cm)
legend_max_size_mm <- 2 * 0.42 * mm_per_unit  # 0.42 = the real pies' max radius (see 1.6/data chunk above)

fig7_top5 <- base_plot +
  geom_point(data = fig7_top5_pie_data, aes(x = x, y = y, size = total), alpha = 0) +
  scale_size_area(
    name = "Isolate number", max_size = legend_max_size_mm, breaks = c(10, 50, 100, round(max_total)),
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, shape = 21, color = "grey40", fill = "grey80"))
  )

fig7_top5
save_apec_plot(fig7_top5, "fig7_top5_variant_piematrix_by_year.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = fig7_width_cm, height = fig7_height_cm)
```

**Pie = production type share; size = isolate count (area-proportional,
calibrated to the real pies' scale - see chunk comments); counts in the
supplementary table above.**

### Fig 8 - Sankey/Alluvial
> based on previous script visuals

#### Top 5 ST example 1 
Carefull data logic for filtering is not the same as fig 7 ! 

- data using top 5 serotypes - and the rest serotype marked as other
- we do also top 5 ST and other ST - so some other serotype might have ST in top 5

- the draw the sankey with panels : year, ST and serotype - color ribon is Production type

```{r grouped columns fig8 ex1}
# Serotype_top5 and ST_top5 are each thresholded independently against the
# full data - unlike Fig 7, where Serotype/ST labels were forced to "Other"
# whenever variant was "Other" (a chained/dependent grouping). Here an
# isolate can be Serotype "Other" while its ST is still one of the top 5 STs,
# or vice versa.
top5_ex1_fig8_prep <-
  isolates %>%
  mutate(
    Serotype_top5 = top_n_other(Serotype, 5, other_label = "Other"),
    ST_top5 = top_n_other(ST, 5, other_label = "Other")
  )
```

Now preparing data for visualisation
```{r getting contingency table for fig8 ex1}
top5_ex1_fig8 <-
  top5_ex1_fig8_prep %>%
  select(Year, ST_top5, Serotype_top5, production_type) %>%
  group_by(Year, ST_top5, Serotype_top5, production_type) %>%
  tally()

top5_ex1_fig8
write_tsv(top5_ex1_fig8, file.path(here::here(params$output_dir), "fig8_ex1_top5ST_serotype_year_tally.tsv"))
```

This is the data we use to produce the figure

Creating the sankey plot:

```{r figure8 ex1 sankey}
fig8_ex1_width_cm <- 26
fig8_ex1_height_cm <- 14
fig8_ex1_box_width <- 1/4  # wider stratum boxes - 1/8 was too narrow for the longer Serotype labels

# ST_top5/Serotype_top5 are thresholded independently (see prep chunk above),
# so "Other" can legitimately occur on both axes for the same isolate. Giving
# each axis its own "Other ST"/"Other Serotype" label avoids ggalluvial
# treating them as the same stratum (its "some strata appear at multiple
# axes" warning) without resorting to discern = TRUE's auto-suffixed labels
# ("Other.1"/"Other.2").
#
# Levels are set kept-categories-first, "Other ST"/"Other Serotype" last, so
# that bucket (secondary information) stacks at the bottom of its axis block
# rather than being interleaved with the named categories.
ST_top5_levels_ex1 <-
  top5_ex1_fig8 %>%
  mutate(ST_top5 = if_else(ST_top5 == "Other", "Other ST", ST_top5)) %>%
  group_by(ST_top5) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(ST_top5)
ST_top5_levels_ex1 <- c(setdiff(ST_top5_levels_ex1, "Other ST"), "Other ST")

Serotype_top5_levels_ex1 <-
  top5_ex1_fig8 %>%
  mutate(Serotype_top5 = if_else(Serotype_top5 == "Other", "Other Serotype", Serotype_top5)) %>%
  group_by(Serotype_top5) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(Serotype_top5)
Serotype_top5_levels_ex1 <- c(setdiff(Serotype_top5_levels_ex1, "Other Serotype"), "Other Serotype")

fig8_ex1_plot_data <-
  top5_ex1_fig8 %>%
  mutate(
    ST_top5 = if_else(ST_top5 == "Other", "Other ST", ST_top5),
    Serotype_top5 = if_else(Serotype_top5 == "Other", "Other Serotype", Serotype_top5),
    ST_top5 = factor(ST_top5, levels = ST_top5_levels_ex1),
    Serotype_top5 = factor(Serotype_top5, levels = Serotype_top5_levels_ex1)
  )

fig8_ex1 <-
  ggplot(
    fig8_ex1_plot_data,
    aes(axis1 = factor(Year), axis2 = ST_top5, axis3 = Serotype_top5, y = n)
  ) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = production_type), width = fig8_ex1_box_width, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_stratum(width = fig8_ex1_box_width, fill = "grey90", color = "grey40") +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Year", "ST", "Serotype"), expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_qual[1:2], name = "Production type") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 ST example 1: isolate flow by Year, ST, Serotype",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of isolates"
  ) +
  theme_apec() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

fig8_ex1
save_apec_plot(fig8_ex1, "fig8_ex1_top5ST_sankey.png", dir = params$figures_dir, width = fig8_ex1_width_cm, height = fig8_ex1_height_cm)
```

#### Top 5 ST example 2

- same logic as example 1 But : 
- display sankey  blocks: production type, year, variant (top5 also and other)
- Ribons top 5 ST + other ST - coloured
So we need new data wrangling then display.
